The honest landscape: roughly 15-25 unique English-language literary-erotica works are reliably PD (Fanny Hill, Venus in Furs, Decameron, Casanova/Machen, Teleny, The Pearl, Romance of Lust, My Secret Life, Sade selections, Frank Harris, Autobiography of a Flea, plus a handful of erotic poetry — Sappho, Catullus, Goethe's Roman Elegies). Three practical paths forward, ranked: (1) BEST: commission a small (~20-50 piece) original fixture corpus from a freelance erotica writer with a work-for-hire / CC0 release — gives voice fidelity, tag fidelity, and unambiguous license. (2) ACCEPTABLE: generate synthetic fixture text with an LLM specifically for fixture-display purposes (clearly labeled as synthetic, not as real content). (3) WORST but cheapest: use the PG corpus for STRUCTURAL fixtures only (chapter counts, word counts, tag density) without ever surfacing the actual prose in UI. Do NOT mix Victorian PD prose into anything a real user would see — it will undermine the contemporary brand. The Standard Ebooks 'we curate PD with editorial polish' model is not a shortcut here because they correctly don't curate erotica. Internet Archive's 'free to read' is a copyright trap, not a source. CC0 modern erotica is essentially a null set."}

Story (schema.prisma:43-80):
- REQUIRED: title (String), content (String), excerpt (String), estimatedReadMinutes (Int).
- Has defaults: accumulatedReadSeconds (BigInt, 0), likeCount (Int, 0), isAuthorsChoice (Boolean, false).
- Optional/nullable: epigraph, authorsNote, publishedAt (set to make public; null = draft), deletedAt.
- Do NOT write: searchVector (Postgres-generated tsvector; Unsupported type).
- Tags via join table StoryTag { storyId, tagId } — composite PK, no extra columns. Nest-create with `tags: { create: tagIds.map(tagId => ({ tagId })) }`.
- notes is a Note[] relation (replaces legacy `notes` string column). Optional.

Series (schema.prisma:86-116):
- REQUIRED: title (String), excerpt (String).
- Has defaults: status (SeriesStatus enum: ONGOING|COMPLETE|HIATUS, default ONGOING), accumulatedReadSeconds, likeCount.
- Optional/nullable: authorsNote, deletedAt.
- Series has NO publishedAt (publish state lives on chapters).
- Tags via SeriesTag { seriesId, tagId } — composite PK.
- Do NOT write: searchVector.

Chapter (schema.prisma:128-161):
- REQUIRED: seriesId (FK -> Series.id), title (String), content (String), excerpt (String), orderIndex (Int — manual, no default; pick max+1 per series), estimatedReadMinutes (Int).
- Has defaults: isAuthorsChoice (false), accumulatedReadSeconds (0), likeCount (0).
- Optional/nullable: epigraph, authorsNote, publishedAt (null = draft), deletedAt.
- Tags via ChapterTag { chapterId, tagId } — composite PK.
- Do NOT write: searchVector.

If seeding via the admin API instead (mirrors seed-content.ts):
- POST /admin/stories (CreateStoryDto, backend/src/stories/dto/create-story.dto.ts): required title, content, excerpt, estimatedReadMinutes; optional isAuthorsChoice, authorsNote, epigraph, tagIds (UUID[]). Then PATCH /admin/stories/:id/publish to publish.
- POST /admin/series (CreateSeriesDto): required title, excerpt; optional authorsNote, status (SeriesStatus), tagIds.
- POST /admin/series/:seriesId/chapters (CreateChapterDto): required title, content, excerpt, estimatedReadMinutes; optional isAuthorsChoice, authorsNote, epigraph, tagIds. orderIndex is NOT in the DTO — assigned server-side. Then PATCH /admin/chapters/:id/publish to publish."}

The animation work in PRs #187–#191 cares about page length and scroll-distance, not semantics, so pure lorem is correct here. estimatedReadMinutes = Math.max(1, Math.round(wordCount / 220)) — 220 wpm is the project's established read-speed constant (matches what the live editor computes)."","codeSkeleton":"/* eslint-disable no-console */
// scripts/seed-dev-content.ts
//
// Synthetic dev-only stress seeder for GSAP animation testing (PRs #187–#191).
// Generates 50 standalone stories + 8 series (3–8 chapters each) with
// faker-driven titles, lorem bodies of 500–10000 words, and tags pulled
// live from the DB. Every row is title-prefixed with the SEED_MARKER so
// --purge can find and wipe ONLY what this script created.
//
// Usage:
//   LUCIFER_ENV=dev npm run seed:dev -- --confirm=dev
//   LUCIFER_ENV=dev npm run seed:dev -- --purge
//   LUCIFER_ENV=dev npm run seed:dev -- --confirm=dev --dry-run
//
// NEVER run this against a non-dev DB. The env-guard and the DATABASE_URL
// sniff are both there for a reason — please leave them alone.

import { config } from 'dotenv';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';
import { PrismaClient, SeriesStatus, Prisma } from '@prisma/client';
import { faker } from '@faker-js/faker';

config({ path: resolve(__dirname, '..', '.env') });

// ── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const SEED_MARKER = '[seed-dev] ';
const WORDS_PER_MINUTE = 220;

const MOOD_NOUNS = [
  'Lamplight', 'Threshold', 'Hollow', 'Cinder', 'Drawer', 'Bell',
  'Mourning', 'Letter', 'Window', 'Doorway', 'Kitchen', 'Garden',
  'Afternoon', 'Evening', 'Stairwell', 'Corridor', 'Page', 'Margin',
  'Silence', 'Weather', 'Rain', 'Snow', 'Coast', 'Hour', 'Pause',
  'Sentence', 'Drawer', 'Coat', 'Glass', 'Promise',
];
const MOOD_ADJS = [
  'Borrowed', 'Hollow', 'Quiet', 'Brittle', 'Late', 'Soft', 'Forgotten',
  'Patient', 'Distant', 'Folded', 'Unspoken', 'Half-Lit', 'Slow',
  'Tender', 'Bruised', 'Gentle', 'Returning', 'Unsent', 'Cold',
  'Yellowed', 'Crumpled', 'Familiar', 'Fragile', 'Honest', 'Plain',
];
const EVOCATIVE_OPENERS = [
  'A meditation on', 'A small confession about', 'Some nights are made of',
  'In the space between', 'A letter never sent about', 'A quiet study of',
  'A few words on', 'Notes toward', 'A scene from', 'A small piece about',
  'The shape of', 'A page from',
];

// ── CLI parsing ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface Flags {
  confirm: boolean;
  purge: boolean;
  dryRun: boolean;
  storiesCount: number;
  seriesCount: number;
  fakerSeed: number;
}

function parseFlags(argv: string[]): Flags {
  if (argv.includes('--help')) {
    printUsage();
    process.exit(0);
  }
  const get = (k: string) => {
    const hit = argv.find((a) => a.startsWith(`${k}=`));
    return hit ? hit.split('=', 2)[1] : undefined;
  };
  return {
    confirm: get('--confirm') === 'dev',
    purge: argv.includes('--purge'),
    dryRun: argv.includes('--dry-run'),
    storiesCount: Number(get('--stories') ?? 50),
    seriesCount: Number(get('--series') ?? 8),
    fakerSeed: Number(get('--seed') ?? Date.now()),
  };
}

function printUsage(): void { /* prints the header comment block */ }

// ── Safety guards ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function assertDevEnv(): void {
  if (process.env.LUCIFER_ENV !== 'dev') {
    console.error(`[seed-dev] LUCIFER_ENV must be "dev" (got: ${process.env.LUCIFER_ENV ?? 'unset'}).`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
  const url = process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? '';
  if (/prod|production|render\.com|neon\.tech/i.test(url)) {
    console.error(`[seed-dev] DATABASE_URL looks production-ish. Refusing.`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

function assertConfirmed(flags: Flags): void {
  if (flags.purge) return; // purge has its own footgun protection
  if (!flags.confirm) {
    console.error(
      '[seed-dev] Pass --confirm=dev to acknowledge this writes synthetic garbage to the DB.',
    );
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

// ── Content generators ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

const usedTitles = new Set<string>();

function generateTitle(): string {
  const templates = [
    () => `The ${pick(MOOD_NOUNS)} of ${faker.person.firstName()}`,
    () => `${pick(MOOD_ADJS)} ${pick(MOOD_NOUNS)}`,
    () => `${titleCase(faker.word.adjective())} ${pick(MOOD_NOUNS)}`,
    () => `After ${pick(MOOD_NOUNS)}`,
  ];
  let base = faker.helpers.arrayElement(templates)();
  let candidate = base;
  let n = 2;
  while (usedTitles.has(candidate)) candidate = `${base} (${n++})`;
  usedTitles.add(candidate);
  return `${SEED_MARKER}${candidate}`;
}

function generateExcerpt(): string {
  const opener = pick(EVOCATIVE_OPENERS);
  const body = faker.lorem.sentences(3);
  const raw = `${opener} ${body.charAt(0).toLowerCase()}${body.slice(1)}`;
  return raw.length > 240 ? raw.slice(0, 237).replace(/\s+\S*$/, '') + '…' : raw;
}

function generateBody(): { content: string; wordCount: number } {
  const target = faker.number.int({ min: 500, max: 10_000 });
  const paragraphs: string[] = [];
  let words = 0;
  while (words < target) {
    const p = faker.lorem.paragraph({ min: 4, max: 9 });
    paragraphs.push(p);
    words += p.split(/\s+/).length;
  }
  return { content: paragraphs.join('\n\n'), wordCount: words };
}

const pick = <T>(arr: readonly T[]) => faker.helpers.arrayElement(arr);
const titleCase = (s: string) => s.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + s.slice(1);

// ── Tag selection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface TagBuckets { safe: { id: string }[]; adult: { id: string }[]; }

async function loadTagBuckets(prisma: PrismaClient): Promise<TagBuckets> {
  const all = await prisma.tag.findMany({ select: { id: true, isAdult: true } });
  return {
    safe: all.filter((t) => !t.isAdult),
    adult: all.filter((t) => t.isAdult),
  };
}

function pickTagIds(buckets: TagBuckets): string[] {
  const want = faker.number.int({ min: 3, max: 6 });
  const ids = new Set<string>();
  let guard = 0;
  while (ids.size < want && guard++ < 50) {
    const pool = faker.number.float() < 0.7 ? buckets.safe : buckets.adult;
    if (!pool.length) continue;
    ids.add(pick(pool).id);
  }
  return [...ids];
}

// ── Date / status helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────

function randomPublishedAt(): Date {
  const sixMonths = 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 30 * 6;
  return new Date(Date.now() - faker.number.int({ min: 0, max: sixMonths }));
}

function randomSeriesStatus(): SeriesStatus {
  return faker.helpers.weightedArrayElement([
    { weight: 60, value: SeriesStatus.ONGOING },
    { weight: 30, value: SeriesStatus.COMPLETE },
    { weight: 10, value: SeriesStatus.HIATUS },
  ]);
}

const isAuthorsChoice = () => faker.number.float() < 0.05;

// ── Existing-rows check ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

async function countExistingSeed(prisma: PrismaClient): Promise<number> {
  const [s, se, c] = await Promise.all([
    prisma.story.count({ where: { title: { startsWith: SEED_MARKER } } }),
    prisma.series.count({ where: { title: { startsWith: SEED_MARKER } } }),
    prisma.chapter.count({ where: { title: { startsWith: SEED_MARKER } } }),
  ]);
  return s + se + c;
}

// ── Purge ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

async function purge(prisma: PrismaClient): Promise<void> {
  const seedSeries = await prisma.series.findMany({
    where: { title: { startsWith: SEED_MARKER } },
    select: { id: true },
  });
  const seriesIds = seedSeries.map((s) => s.id);

  const result = await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
    const chapters = await tx.chapter.deleteMany({
      where: { OR: [
        { title: { startsWith: SEED_MARKER } },
        { seriesId: { in: seriesIds } },
      ] },
    });
    const series = await tx.series.deleteMany({ where: { title: { startsWith: SEED_MARKER } } });
    const stories = await tx.story.deleteMany({ where: { title: { startsWith: SEED_MARKER } } });
    return { chapters, series, stories };
  });

  console.log(
    `[seed-dev] purged: ${result.stories.count} stories, ${result.series.count} series, ${result.chapters.count} chapters`,
  );
  console.warn('[seed-dev] note: polymorphic likes/saves/reading-positions are NOT auto-cleaned (no FK). Inspect manually if needed.');
}

// ── Seed planner ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface PlannedStory { title: string; excerpt: string; content: string; wordCount: number; tagIds: string[]; }
interface PlannedSeries { title: string; excerpt: string; status: SeriesStatus; tagIds: string[]; chapters: Array<PlannedStory & { orderIndex: number }>; }

function planStories(buckets: TagBuckets, n: number): PlannedStory[] {
  return Array.from({ length: n }, () => {
    const { content, wordCount } = generateBody();
    return {
      title: generateTitle(),
      excerpt: generateExcerpt(),
      content,
      wordCount,
      tagIds: pickTagIds(buckets),
    };
  });
}

function planSeries(buckets: TagBuckets, n: number): PlannedSeries[] {
  return Array.from({ length: n }, () => {
    const chapterCount = faker.number.int({ min: 3, max: 8 });
    return {
      title: generateTitle(),
      excerpt: generateExcerpt(),
      status: randomSeriesStatus(),
      tagIds: pickTagIds(buckets),
      chapters: Array.from({ length: chapterCount }, (_, i) => {
        const { content, wordCount } = generateBody();
        return {
          title: generateTitle(),
          excerpt: generateExcerpt(),
          content,
          wordCount,
          tagIds: pickTagIds(buckets),
          orderIndex: i,
        };
      }),
    };
  });
}

// ── Insert (transactional) ───────────────────────────────────────────────

async function insertAll(prisma: PrismaClient, stories: PlannedStory[], series: PlannedSeries[]): Promise<void> {
  await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
    for (const s of stories) {
      const created = await tx.story.create({
        data: {
          title: s.title,
          content: s.content,
          excerpt: s.excerpt,
          estimatedReadMinutes: Math.max(1, Math.round(s.wordCount / WORDS_PER_MINUTE)),
          isAuthorsChoice: isAuthorsChoice(),
          publishedAt: randomPublishedAt(),
        },
        select: { id: true },
      });
      if (s.tagIds.length) {
        await tx.storyTag.createMany({
          data: s.tagIds.map((tagId) => ({ storyId: created.id, tagId })),
          skipDuplicates: true,
        });
      }
    }

    for (const se of series) {
      const created = await tx.series.create({
        data: { title: se.title, excerpt: se.excerpt, status: se.status },
        select: { id: true },
      });
      if (se.tagIds.length) {
        await tx.seriesTag.createMany({
          data: se.tagIds.map((tagId) => ({ seriesId: created.id, tagId })),
          skipDuplicates: true,
        });
      }
      for (const ch of se.chapters) {
        const chCreated = await tx.chapter.create({
          data: {
            seriesId: created.id,
            title: ch.title,
            content: ch.content,
            excerpt: ch.excerpt,
            orderIndex: ch.orderIndex,
            estimatedReadMinutes: Math.max(1, Math.round(ch.wordCount / WORDS_PER_MINUTE)),
            isAuthorsChoice: isAuthorsChoice(),
            publishedAt: randomPublishedAt(),
          },
          select: { id: true },
        });
        if (ch.tagIds.length) {
          await tx.chapterTag.createMany({
            data: ch.tagIds.map((tagId) => ({ chapterId: chCreated.id, tagId })),
            skipDuplicates: true,
          });
        }
      }
    }
  }, { timeout: 120_000 });
}

// ── Dry-run reporter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function reportDryRun(stories: PlannedStory[], series: PlannedSeries[]): void {
  const totalChapters = series.reduce((acc, s) => acc + s.chapters.length, 0);
  console.log('[seed-dev] DRY RUN — would insert:');
  console.log(`  stories:  ${stories.length}`);
  console.log(`  series:   ${series.length}`);
  console.log(`  chapters: ${totalChapters}`);
  console.log('[seed-dev] first 5 story titles:');
  stories.slice(0, 5).forEach((s) => console.log(`  - ${s.title} (${s.wordCount} words)`));
  console.log('[seed-dev] first 5 series titles:');
  series.slice(0, 5).forEach((s) => console.log(`  - ${s.title} (${s.chapters.length} chapters, status=${s.status})`));
}

// ── Main ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const flags = parseFlags(process.argv.slice(2));
  assertDevEnv();

  faker.seed(flags.fakerSeed);
  console.log(`[seed-dev] faker seed: ${flags.fakerSeed}`);

  const prisma = new PrismaClient();
  try {
    if (flags.purge) {
      await purge(prisma);
      return;
    }
    assertConfirmed(flags);

    const existing = await countExistingSeed(prisma);
    if (existing > 0) {
      console.error(`[seed-dev] found ${existing} pre-existing seed rows. Run --purge first.`);
      process.exit(1);
    }

    const buckets = await loadTagBuckets(prisma);
    if (!buckets.safe.length && !buckets.adult.length) {
      console.error('[seed-dev] no tags in DB. Run `npm run seed:tags` first.');
      process.exit(1);
    }

    const stories = planStories(buckets, flags.storiesCount);
    const series = planSeries(buckets, flags.seriesCount);

    if (flags.dryRun) {
      reportDryRun(stories, series);
      return;
    }

    console.log('[seed-dev] inserting…');
    await insertAll(prisma, stories, series);
    const totalCh = series.reduce((a, s) => a + s.chapters.length, 0);
    console.log(`[seed-dev] done: ${stories.length} stories, ${series.length} series, ${totalCh} chapters.`);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error('[seed-dev] runtime error:', err);
    process.exit(2);
  } finally {
    await prisma.$disconnect();
  }
}

void main();"}

Output a JSON object with these fields:
- summary: 2-3 sentences capturing the headline finding (e.g. "PD pool exists but it's X works, Y era, Z fit — synthetic is more aligned with the test goal").
- pdOption: { viable: boolean, volume: string, voiceFit: string, fitForGSAPTesting: string, recommendation: "use" | "skip" | "use-some" }. Be honest.

input.summary: The verified public-domain erotica pool is real but tiny (~15-25 unique English titles), almost entirely pre-1930, and reads as florid Victorian/Enlightenment euphemism with consent vocabularies that range from absent to actively offensive — using any of it in UI fixtures would actively undermine the contemporary slow-burn-literary brand. For the actual test goal (stressing GSAP scroll animations across PRs #187-#191, which care about page length and scroll distance, not prose semantics), a synthetic faker-driven seeder is both safer and more fit-for-purpose. The synthetic plan is fully spec'd, safety-guarded, idempotent, and ready to ship as a single PR.

pdOption.volume: ~15-25 unique English-language literary-erotica works total across PG bookshelves 33 + 703, Wikisource, and PDR. Modern CC0/PD erotica is effectively a null set. Anything on Internet Archive labeled 'free to read' that isn't sourced from PG is in-copyright and a DMCA trap.
pdOption.voiceFit: Bad. Every usable title is pre-1930, most are Victorian or earlier (Fanny Hill 1748, Venus in Furs 1870, Decameron 1350s, Teleny 1893, The Pearl 1879). Voice is florid period euphemism that reads as parody to contemporary eyes and clashes with the Garth-Greenwell/Mary-Gaitskill register the site is going for. Consent and queer-affirming vocabularies are absent; several titles (The Pearl, Venus in India, Moorish Harem) carry colonial-fetish and non-consent content that's ethically fraught to surface in any UI.
pdOption.fitForGSAPTesting: Mediocre even on the narrow technical goal. GSAP work cares about page length, scroll distance, and tag-density spread across stories/series/chapters — not prose authenticity. PD bodies exist (Decameron, Casanova/Machen) but ingestion, cleanup, and chunking into chapter-shaped units is meaningful engineering for content that you'd then have to hide from the UI anyway because it's brand-toxic. Synthetic lorem of controlled length hits the same animation surface with zero ingestion overhead.

syntheticOption.fileSummary: Single new file at backend/scripts/seed-dev-content.ts following the existing seed:* convention (sibling of seed-tags.ts and seed-content.ts, ts-node --transpile-only, idempotent main()/catch/disconnect lifecycle). Adds @faker-js/faker as a devDependency in backend/package.json and a `seed:dev` script entry. No schema migration — the [seed-dev] title prefix is the marker, so purge is a trivial startsWith filter.
syntheticOption.volumeSummary: 50 standalone stories + 8 series with 3-8 chapters each (averages ~44 chapters, within the 40-60 envelope). Each body is 500-10,000 words uniform-random to give the GSAP scroll work a healthy spread of short/medium/long pages. Tags pulled live from the DB's 591-tag taxonomy: 3-6 per row, 70/30 safe/adult mix so the distribution matches the rough real-site shape. Titles are hand-pooled mood words combined with faker — brand-aligned, never copied. Bodies are pure faker.lorem because animation work doesn't care about semantics.
syntheticOption.safetySummary: Three independent guards: (1) hard refuse unless LUCIFER_ENV=dev, (2) sniff DATABASE_URL for prod/production/render.com/neon.tech and abort if matched, (3) require --confirm=dev on every seed run. Idempotent — refuses to seed if [seed-dev] rows already exist, points operator at --purge. --purge wipes ONLY rows whose title starts with [seed-dev] (Story/Series/Chapter), inside a single transaction, with cascades handling junction tables. --dry-run prints counts + first 5 titles per type with zero writes. All inserts wrapped in one prisma.$transaction (120s timeout) so a mid-run crash leaves zero partial rows. Strict exit codes: 0 success, 1 guard failure, 2 runtime error.
syntheticOption.runCommand: cd backend && LUCIFER_ENV=dev npm run seed:dev -- --confirm=dev
syntheticOption.purgeCommand: cd backend && LUCIFER_ENV=dev npm run seed:dev -- --purge

whatBuildLooksLike: Add @faker-js/faker to backend/package.json devDependencies (npm i -D @faker-js/faker in backend/) and a new `seed:dev` script entry pointing at scripts/seed-dev-content.ts via ts-node --transpile-only.

Create /Users/taha/Claude projects/LucifersDiary/backend/scripts/seed-dev-content.ts implementing the full skeleton: CLI parsing, three safety guards (LUCIFER_ENV, DATABASE_URL sniff, --confirm=dev), tag-bucket loader, planners for stories/series/chapters, transactional insert, --purge path, --dry-run reporter.
Zero schema changes — the [seed-dev] title prefix is the marker, exported as a top-level SEED_MARKER constant so seed and purge can't drift.
No changes to existing seed-tags.ts or seed-content.ts — this is a new sibling script with its own namespace.

After merge the user runs (from backend/): LUCIFER_ENV=dev npm run seed:dev -- --confirm=dev to populate, --dry-run to preview, --purge to wipe. Then opens the GSAP-scroll PRs against a DB with 50 stories + 8 series + ~44 chapters of varied length.
Optional follow-ups (out of scope for this PR): a tiny docs/dev-seeding.md note pointing at the script, and a CI guard that fails if anyone tries to import @faker-js/faker outside scripts/.
openQuestionsForUser: Keep the default counts (50 stories / 8 series / 3-8 chapters each) or push higher for heavier scroll-stress?
Should the script also seed a handful of draft (publishedAt=null) rows so the admin draft views are exercised, or published-only as currently specced?
Lock in the [seed-dev] title prefix as the marker, or would you rather a less-visible tag (e.g. a specific authorsNote sentinel) so the prefix doesn't appear if a screenshot leaks?
